scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Jazz dance originated in early 20th-century African American communities in the United States, evolving from vernacular social dances such as the shimmy, Charleston, and Lindy hop.
The shimmy, inspired by Spencer Williams's 1917 song, involved rapid shoulder movements.
The Charleston featured toes-in, heels-out twisting steps, and the Lindy hop was a rhythmically conscious partner dance.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Jazz dance originated as social entertainment within African American communities and became a form of cultural expression and resistance.
It provided joy and communal connection during difficult times such as the Great Depression.
Theatrical jazz dance conveys narrative, character, and emotion in musicals and films.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Jazz dance is performed with a grounded posture emphasizing torso mobility and parallel foot positions.
Early vernacular jazz included solo and partner dances like the Charleston and Lindy hop, featuring twisting steps and rhythmically spontaneous partner work.
Theatrical jazz incorporates codified techniques with contractions, isolations, and expressive gestures.
Watch for Shimmy, Charleston Step, Torso Isolation.

Formation: flexible formations: solo, partner, or group; spatial use varies by style

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Jazz dance is closely tied to jazz music, characterized by syncopation, improvisation, and rhythmic complexity.
Early jazz dance was performed to ragtime and swing music.
Listen for the piano, brass (trumpet, trombone), drums, double bass.
The pulse is 4/4 with syncopation at about 130 beats a minute.
Jazz dance music features syncopated rhythms with swung eighth notes, driven by piano, brass, and drums, creating an energetic and improvisational sound that supports expressive, rhythmic movement.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Costumes vary by style and era, from casual social dance attire in early vernacular jazz to theatrical costumes in Broadway jazz and film.
Early social dances were performed in everyday clothing suitable for dance halls and clubs.
Theatrical jazz uses stylized costumes reflecting character and mood, often incorporating hats, gloves, and tailored suits or dresses.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Key figures include Jack Cole, who popularized theatrical jazz; Bob Fosse, known for his distinctive, suggestive choreography; Katherine Dunham, who introduced isolations and anthropological insights; Eugene Louis Faccuito (Luigi), creator of the first codified jazz technique; Gus Giordano, noted for clean, precise movement; and Patsy Swayze, who combined jazz and ballet.
Jazz dance styles vary regionally and historically.
Jazz dance descends from African American vernacular dances of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, incorporating elements of African, European, and Caribbean dance traditions.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Jazz dance is parent of Charleston: An early vernacular jazz dance characterized by twisting footwork.
Jazz dance is parent of Lindy hop: A rhythmically complex partner dance foundational to jazz dance.
Jazz dance is shares music of Hip-hop: Commercial jazz incorporates elements of hip-hop music and movement.
Jazz dance is shares music of Breaking: Street jazz and breaking share urban dance influences.

wardrobe.from_sources: Costumes vary by style and era, from casual social dance attire in early vernacular jazz to theatrical costumes in Broadway jazz and film. Early social dances were performed in everyday clothing suitable for dance halls and clubs. Theatrical jazz uses stylized costumes reflecting character and mood, often incorporating hats, gloves, and tailored suits or dresses. Contemporary jazz costumes are diverse, ranging from streetwear in commercial jazz to sleek, form-fitting attire in stage performances. Settings include social dance venues, theaters, television studios, and dance competitions.
